text: Introduction Did you know that indoor air can be 2 to 5 times more polluted than outdoor air? According to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), people spend nearly 90% of their time indoors, constantly exposed to hidden pollutants trapped in carpets, upholstery, and air systems. The result is a cleaner, healthier indoor environment for your family. The Truth About Carpets and Indoor Air Quality Are Carpets Really Bad for Air Quality? There is a common myth that carpets harm indoor air quality. However, studies from the Carpet & Rug Institute show that clean carpets actually help improve air quality by trapping allergens like: Dust Pollen Pet dander Airborne particles When properly maintained, carpets act like a natural air filter , preventing these pollutants from circulating in your home. Additionally, the problem begins when carpets are neglected. Over time, trapped particles build up and can be released back into the air every time you walk across the floor. Why Carpet Cleaning Matters for Indoor Air Vacuuming Alone Is Not Enough Vacuuming is important, but it only removes surface-level dirt. In fact, even high-quality vacuums can only remove about 80–95% of dry debris , leaving deep contaminants behind. Hidden deep inside carpet fibers are: Dust mites Bacteria Mold spores Allergens To fully improve air quality, professional deep cleaning is necessary. How Professional Carpet Cleaning Improves Air Quality Professional carpet cleaning in Lake Forest uses advanced methods like hot water extraction to remove deeply embedded contaminants. Key Benefits: Removes trapped allergens and bacteria Eliminates dust mites and pollutants Reduces mold growth caused by moisture Improves airflow inside your home Creates a fresher indoor environment At Carpet & Duct Cleaning, we use eco-friendly, non-toxic solutions that are safe for children, pets, and sensitive individuals. Furthermore, unlike store-bought detergents that leave residue, our cleaning process ensures carpets are fully rinsed and residue-free. Professional Carpet Cleaning Methods Explained 1. Hot Water Extraction (Steam Cleaning) This is the most effective and recommended method by carpet manufacturers. It works by: Injecting hot water deep into carpet fibers Breaking down dirt, bacteria, and allergens Extracting everything using powerful suction Benefits: Deep sanitization Removes allergens and pollutants Extends carpet lifespan No harmful chemical residue 2. Dry Cleaning Uses minimal moisture and special compounds to attract dirt. Best for: Delicate carpets Quick cleaning situations However, it does not remove deeply embedded allergens as effectively as steam cleaning. 3. Bonnet Cleaning A surface-level method using a rotating pad. Moreover, while it improves appearance, it does not significantly improve air quality because it does not clean deep fibers. Carpet Cleaning + Air Duct Cleaning = Maximum Air Quality Carpets are not the only source of indoor pollutants. Your HVAC system and air ducts also circulate dust, mold, and allergens throughout your home. That’s why combining: Carpet cleaning Air duct cleaning creates a complete indoor air improvement system . This combination helps: Reduce airborne allergens Improve HVAC efficiency Enhance overall breathing quality We recommend: Carpet cleaning every 6–12 months Air duct cleaning every 3–5 years How Dirty Carpets Affect Your Health Unclean carpets can directly impact your well-being. Common Health Effects: Increased allergy symptoms Asthma flare-ups Respiratory irritation Sneezing and coughing Poor sleep quality If symptoms improve when you leave your home, your carpet may be a hidden trigger. Schedule your service now and breathe cleaner, healthier air in your home. FAQ How does carpet cleaning improve indoor air quality? It removes dust, allergens, bacteria, and pollutants trapped deep in carpet fibers. How often should carpets be cleaned? Every 6–12 months for most homes, or more frequently if you have pets or allergies. Is steam cleaning safe for indoor air quality? Yes, hot water extraction is one of the safest and most effective cleaning methods. Can dirty carpets cause allergies? Yes, dust mites and allergens in carpets can trigger asthma and allergy symptoms. Do carpets really trap allergens? Yes, carpets act as filters by trapping airborne particles until they are removed through cleaning.
